dossier.public_summary: The signal is strong but odd and even dips have very different depths, which a planet should not show. The dip is also much longer and more grazing than expected for this small star, and there is extra light variation between dips. Together this best matches an eclipsing stellar binary seen at half its true period, not a transiting planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits have very different depths (depth_odd_ppm 14900 vs depth_even_ppm 3100, depth_difference 0.792, depth_ratio 4.8). This 5.6-sigma odd/even difference with a depth change of 11800 ppm is strong evidence for an eclipsing binary folded at half its true period (27.8 d) or for two very different eclipses, not a planet with equal transits.

Observed duration 2.999 h vs central_h 1.913 h gives ratio 1.567 and fit_b 0.8351. Combined with star_density_penalty 62.98 and fit_log_density_ratio -1.948, the transit is too long and too grazing for a central planet on this 0.2758 Rsun M dwarf, favoring a stellar eclipse geometry.

There is a measurable out-of-transit signal at this period (phase_curve amplitude 1586 ppm, 13.8% of dip depth) with chi2 16.87/9, consistent with ellipsoidal or spot modulation from a close binary, supporting the EB interpretation over a planet despite a flat bottom (shape v_sigma -3.353).
